text:
Stress and ADHD draw on the same part of the brain. The prefrontal cortex supports attention, working memory, inhibition and emotion regulation, and ongoing stress is associated with poorer prefrontal function. Stimulant medication is associated with better attention, inhibition and working memory. On current evidence, it does not normalise emotion regulation or reduce the demands stress brings. When things start slipping, rising stress is worth exploring. Asking what has changed in the load can point to other levers, such as adjusting demands and building skills. Any medication change is a conversation with the prescriber.

Where the evidence stops:
• Much of the stress detail comes from animal studies, with human findings pointing the same way.
• Findings on medication and emotion regulation are limited.

Key sources:
• Isfandnia et al., 2024: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neubiorev.2024.105703
• Lenzi et al., 2018: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neubiorev.2017.08.010
